content: The World Health Organization (WHO) Technical Report Series No. 972 focuses on research priorities for helminth infections, which affect over a billion people in sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, and the Americas. These infections contribute to significant morbidity, perpetuating cycles of poverty, reduced productivity, and inadequate socioeconomic development. The report evaluates current research and challenges in controlling helminthiases of public health importance, including onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis, soil-transmitted helminthiases, schistosomiasis, food-borne trematodiases, and taeniasis/cysticercosis. The evaluation is structured around five major themes: intervention strategies, epidemiology and surveillance, environmental and social ecology, data and modeling, and fundamental biology. Despite recent advancements in tools for helminth control and some progress in research capacity, significant gaps remain in diagnostic tools, control measures, and fundamental understanding of helminth biology and transmission dynamics. Additionally, there are deficiencies in health research capacity and policy development. The report identifies opportunities to improve disease control and reduce poverty, offering recommendations to inform public health policy, guide implementation programs, and focus the research community on addressing the needs of disease control and human welfare improvement. These recommendations aim to support national health strategies and address pressing public health concerns globally. The WHO, established in 1948, serves as the directing and coordinating authority for international health matters. Through its publications, WHO provides objective and reliable information to support health strategies and address global health challenges. The organization emphasizes the dissemination of knowledge and collaboration with member countries and global health leaders to promote health, prevent disease, and achieve the highest possible level of health for all people. The WHO Technical Report Series disseminates findings from international expert groups, providing the latest scientific and technical advice on medical and public health subjects. These experts serve in their personal capacities, and their views do not necessarily reflect WHO's policies. The report on helminth infections represents the collective views of an international group of experts and highlights the need for continued research and innovation to address the challenges posed by these neglected tropical diseases.
